newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prices firm on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prices firm on speculative buying.

text.p: U.S. West Coast refined product prices firmed modestly Friday afternoon, fueled in part by speculative buying in the wake of the late-Thursday fire at Mobil's Los Angeles-area refinery.

The fire, located in a coker at the 130,000 barrel per day refinery, was seen more likely to boost distillate prices than gasoline, which remained steady in late trade ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"I think there's been some speculative buying from traders," one broker said of the fire's impact on the market late in the day.

Low sulphur diesel for prompt deliveries in Los Angeles was bid 69.0 cents a gallon, asked 70 cents, rising half a cent a gallon on the day. Prompt CARB diesel buyers were at 71 cents a gallon looking for sellers.
Regular unleaded in Los Angeles gave back 0.50 cent a gallon, at 60.50 cents a gallon bid, 61.50 cents asked in Los Angeles. Premium remained 4.50 cents higher.
CARB gasoline was steady at 64 cents a gallon bid, 65 cents asked in Los Angeles, with CARB premium 3 cents higher.
